us-eo14028.status: In force (partially amended by subsequent executive orders)
us-eo14028.scope: Companies that supply software to the U.S. federal government. Section 4 (Enhancing Software Supply Chain Security) is the basis for requiring SBOMs, secure development practices and vulnerability disclosure
dates: Certain provisions amended by EO 14306 (including attestation validation provisions; to be verified)

us-eo14028-sbom.title: Provide an SBOM to purchasers
us-eo14028-sbom.text: Provide a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) for each product directly to the purchaser or publish it on a public website.

actions.dev: Generate an SBOM (CycloneDX/SPDX) for every build and attach it to the release
actions.admin: Retain SBOMs per product and version and manage the delivery channel to customers
actions.sales: Specify the SBOM delivery method (portal download) in proposals and contracts

us-eo14028-ssdf.title: Follow and attest to secure software development practices
us-eo14028-ssdf.text: Secure development environments, maintain code integrity and check for vulnerabilities in line with the NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF), and attest to conformity upon request.

actions.dev: Keep evidence for each SSDF practice (build signatures, vulnerability scan records)
actions.admin: Retain attestation submission history and supporting evidence
actions.sales: Track the schedule of federal customers' self-attestation requests

us-eo14028-vdp.title: Operate a vulnerability disclosure program
us-eo14028-vdp.text: Operate a vulnerability disclosure program (VDP) process that accepts external reports.

actions.dev: Publish analysis results of reported vulnerabilities as VEX
actions.admin: Operate a security point of contact (e.g. security.txt) and handling deadlines
actions.sales: Direct customers to the vulnerability reporting channel when they inquire

us-ssdf.status: In force (v1.1). Revision in progress — check for the latest version
us-ssdf.scope: Basis for the federal procurement self-attestation form. Also widely used in the private sector as a benchmark for assessing secure development maturity

ssdf-ps1.title: Protect code from unauthorized changes
ssdf-ps1.text: Protect all forms of code from unauthorized access and tampering.

actions.dev: Protected branches, mandatory reviews and signed commits in repositories
actions.admin: Minimize and periodically review access rights to repositories and build servers

ssdf-ps2.title: Provide a mechanism for verifying release integrity
ssdf-ps2.text: Enable software acquirers to verify the integrity of software releases (hashes, signatures).

actions.dev: Attach signatures (cosign/notation) to release artifacts
actions.admin: Operate signing key custody and rotation procedures; distribute public keys
actions.sales: Explain to customers how to verify signatures

ssdf-ps3.title: Archive releases and component provenance (SBOM)
ssdf-ps3.text: Archive each software release and collect, maintain and share provenance data for its components (SBOM).

actions.dev: Generate and attach an SBOM for each release, populating component identifiers (purl)
actions.admin: Retain releases and SBOMs long term

ssdf-pw4.title: Verify reused software
ssdf-pw4.text: Verify external and open source components before adoption and during use (vulnerabilities, licenses, support status).

actions.dev: Check vulnerabilities, licenses and end of support when adding new dependencies

ssdf-rv1.title: Identify vulnerabilities on an ongoing basis
ssdf-rv1.text: Continue to identify and confirm component vulnerabilities after release.

actions.admin: Keep the vulnerability database up to date and re-analyze periodically

ssdf-rv2.title: Assess, prioritize and remediate vulnerabilities
ssdf-rv2.text: Assess vulnerabilities, prioritize them and remediate them.

actions.dev: Patch KEV and publicly exploited vulnerabilities first; record non-affected cases in VEX with justification
actions.sales: Share impact status with customers via VEX

us-attestation.status: In force (operation after EO 14306 in 2025 to be verified)
us-attestation.scope: Producers of software used by federal agencies. The CEO or a designee attests by signature to conformity in four SSDF-based areas

att-env.title: Secure development environments
att-env.text: Separate and protect development and build environments, and control and log access to them.

actions.dev: Separate build environments and enforce multi-factor authentication
actions.sales: Confirm the attestation signatory and submission schedule

att-supply.title: Trusted source code supply chains
att-supply.text: Manage the provenance of internal and external code and use automated tools to check supply chain risks.

actions.dev: Pin dependency sources (lock files) and produce an SBOM

att-provenance.title: Maintain component provenance
att-provenance.text: Maintain provenance data for internal code and third-party components.

actions.dev: Populate supplier and identifier fields in the SBOM

att-vuln.title: Vulnerability checking and remediation
att-vuln.text: Check for vulnerabilities before and after release and address them through a disclosure process.

actions.dev: Zero vulnerabilities before release, or VEX justification

us-sbom-min.name: NTIA Minimum Elements for an SBOM (including CISA update work)
us-sbom-min.status: In force (2021). CISA revision (adding component hashes, licenses, etc.) in draft — finalization to be verified
us-sbom-min.scope: All suppliers providing SBOMs. Cited as the SBOM quality benchmark in federal procurement, FDA submissions and private contracts
dates: CISA revised draft released (to be verified)

sbom-min-fields.title: Required data fields
sbom-min-fields.text: Supplier name, component name, version, unique identifier (e.g. purl), dependency relationship, author of SBOM data, timestamp.

actions.dev: Confirm that the SBOM generation tool populates supplier, purl and timestamp

sbom-min-format.title: Machine-readable format
sbom-min-format.text: A standard machine-readable format such as SPDX or CycloneDX.

actions.dev: Output in CycloneDX 1.5 or later, or SPDX 2.3 or later

sbom-min-practice.title: Update frequency and distribution
sbom-min-practice.text: Update the SBOM with every new build or release, explicitly identify unknown components, and define the distribution method and access control.

actions.dev: Make SBOM generation a fixed step in the build pipeline
actions.admin: Manage SBOM access rights per customer
actions.sales: Specify SBOM scope and delivery method in contracts

us-fda-524b.scope: Premarket submissions for medical devices that include software and can connect to the internet (cyber devices)
dates: FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance finalized (check for later revisions)

fda-sbom.title: Submit an SBOM
fda-sbom.text: Submit an SBOM including commercial, open source and off-the-shelf software components. The guidance also expects the level of support and end-of-support date for each component.

actions.dev: Add support status and end-of-support date for each component to the SBOM
actions.admin: Maintain a list of EOL components
actions.sales: Account for SBOM submission in the regulatory submission timeline

fda-postmarket.title: Postmarket vulnerability management plan
fda-postmarket.text: Submit a plan to monitor, identify and address postmarket vulnerabilities (including coordinated vulnerability disclosure).

actions.dev: Document vulnerability analysis and VEX publication procedures
actions.admin: Operate periodic re-analysis and customer notification
actions.sales: Explain the security advisory process to hospital customers

fda-update.title: Provide updates and patches
fda-update.text: Maintain processes to design, develop and maintain the device for reasonable assurance, and provide means to deliver regular and emergency (out-of-cycle) updates.

actions.dev: Distribute signed updates

us-cmmc.status: In force — contract clauses being phased in
us-cmmc.scope: Defense contractors and subcontractors handling Federal Contract Information (FCI) or Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI)
dates: DFARS contract clause Phase 1 effective (to be verified)

cmmc-l2.title: 110 NIST SP 800-171 security requirements
cmmc-l2.text: Contractors handling CUI implement the 110 requirements of NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 2 and undergo assessment (self or third-party).

actions.admin: Manage 800-171 implementation status and SPRS score
actions.sales: Check the required level in solicitations and address flow-down clauses

cmmc-sc.title: Flow-down of requirements to subcontractors
cmmc-sc.text: CMMC requirements are flowed down to subcontractors by contract.

actions.admin: Verify the security posture of partner companies
actions.sales: Confirm the prime contractor's required level before contracting

us-cybertrust.name: U.S. Cyber Trust Mark (FCC IoT security label)
us-cybertrust.status: Operating (changes to administrator and schedule to be verified)
us-cybertrust.scope: Consumer wireless IoT products. Security criteria based on NIST IR 8425

ctm-support.title: Disclose updates and support period
ctm-support.text: Disclose to consumers whether security updates are provided and the support period.

actions.dev: Implement a security update mechanism
actions.sales: Use label status in marketing

eu-cra.status: In force — applying in phases (reporting obligations apply)
eu-cra.scope: Manufacturers, importers and distributors of products with digital elements (hardware and software) placed on the EU market. Products covered by separate rules such as medical devices and motor vehicles are excluded
dates: Provisions on conformity assessment bodies apply

cra-a1p1.title: Product security requirements
cra-a1p1.text: Placed on the market without known exploitable vulnerabilities, secure by default configuration, security update mechanism, access control, data protection, minimized attack surface, recording of security events.

actions.dev: Confirm zero KEV and publicly exploited vulnerabilities before release; secure defaults
actions.admin: Include vulnerability criteria in release decision criteria

cra-a1p2-1.title: Draw up an SBOM
cra-a1p2-1.text: Draw up an SBOM in a commonly used, machine-readable format covering at least the top-level dependencies.

actions.dev: Generate an SBOM for every release (BSI TR-03183-2 fields recommended)
actions.admin: Include and retain the SBOM in the technical documentation
actions.sales: Prepare a procedure for providing it on request from market surveillance authorities

cra-a1p2-2.title: Address vulnerabilities without delay and provide free security updates
cra-a1p2-2.text: Address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay, and provide security updates free of charge, separately from functionality updates where technically feasible.

actions.dev: Set up the ability to ship security patches as separate releases
actions.sales: Distinguish maintenance contracts from the obligation to provide free security updates

cra-a1p2-5.title: Coordinated vulnerability disclosure and contact address
cra-a1p2-5.text: Publicly disclose information about fixed vulnerabilities, and put in place a coordinated vulnerability disclosure (CVD) policy and a contact address for reporting.

actions.dev: Disclose fixed vulnerabilities via VEX and security advisories
actions.admin: Publish the CVD policy and contact address
actions.sales: Invite customers to subscribe to security advisories

cra-a13-8.title: Support period (at least 5 years as a rule)
cra-a13-8.text: Determine the support period reflecting the expected time the product is in use (at least 5 years as a rule), and handle vulnerabilities throughout that period.

actions.dev: Choose components usable for the whole support period (avoid EOL)
actions.sales: State the support period in product information and contracts

cra-a14.title: Report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents
cra-a14.text: On becoming aware of an actively exploited vulnerability: early warning within 24 hours, vulnerability notification within 72 hours, and final report within 14 days after a corrective measure is available (via the ENISA single reporting platform). Severe incidents: 24 hours, 72 hours and 1 month.

actions.dev: Escalate immediately to the reporting process when a KEV-listed vulnerability is assessed as affecting the product
actions.admin: Designate a 24-hour reporting owner and procedure
actions.sales: Prepare customer notification templates

cra-a2.title: Information and instructions to the user
cra-a2.text: Provide the manufacturer's contact details, the vulnerability reporting point of contact, the end date of the support period, instructions for secure installation and updates, and (where made available) the location of the SBOM.

actions.dev: Document security settings and update procedures
actions.sales: Publish the end-of-support date on product pages

cra-a13-tech.title: Technical documentation, declaration of conformity and CE marking
cra-a13-tech.text: Draw up technical documentation including the cybersecurity risk assessment and keep it for 10 years, draw up the EU declaration of conformity and affix the CE marking.

actions.dev: Produce risk assessment and test records
actions.sales: Provide the declaration of conformity to importers and distributors

eu-bsi-tr03183.authority: Federal Office for Information Security (BSI), Germany
eu-bsi-tr03183.binding: Recommended (cited as a CRA implementation benchmark)
eu-bsi-tr03183.status: In force (v2 series — latest version number to be verified)
eu-bsi-tr03183.scope: German technical guideline specifying format and mandatory fields of SBOMs for the CRA. Required by European customers as an SBOM quality benchmark

tr03183-format.title: SBOM format and version
tr03183-format.text: Provide CycloneDX or SPDX at or above the specified version (differs by edition — check the original text) in JSON/XML.

actions.dev: Output in CycloneDX 1.6 / SPDX 2.3 or later

tr03183-fields.title: Mandatory component fields
tr03183-fields.text: Creator and timestamp; per component: creator, name, version, filename, dependencies, licence, hash of the executable (SHA-512), etc.

actions.dev: Complete license, hash and supplier fields (target 0% missing)
actions.sales: Confirm European customers' SBOM quality requirements

eu-nis2.status: In force (progress of transposition by Member States to be verified)
eu-nis2.scope: Essential and important entities in the EU (energy, transport, banking, health, digital infrastructure, etc.). Suppliers receive customers' supply chain security requirements through contracts

nis2-21d.title: Supply chain security
nis2-21d.text: Customer entities assess suppliers' security level and development practices and reflect them in contracts.

actions.admin: Prepare materials for customer security questionnaires (SBOM, VEX, signatures)
actions.sales: Check security clauses in contracts with EU public-sector and infrastructure customers

nis2-23.title: Incident reporting (24 hours, 72 hours, 1 month)
nis2-23.text: Because customer entities must report significant incidents, they require prompt incident notification from suppliers.

actions.sales: Check contractual notification deadlines

eu-dora.binding: Mandatory (financial entities) → contractual requirements on ICT providers
eu-dora.scope: EU financial entities and their ICT third-party service providers

dora-28.title: ICT third-party risk and contractual provisions
dora-28.text: Financial entities include security, audit and termination provisions in contracts with ICT providers and maintain a register of information.

actions.admin: Procedure for audit cooperation and providing security evidence
actions.sales: Review DORA clauses in contracts with EU financial customers

eu-pld.scope: Software is included as a product. Failure to provide security updates may be deemed a defect
dates: Transposition deadline (applies to products placed on the market thereafter)

pld-update.title: Liability for providing security updates
pld-update.text: Failure to provide software updates (including security updates) within the manufacturer's control is a factor in assessing defectiveness.

actions.dev: Provide security patches within the support period
actions.sales: Have legal review contractual limitation-of-liability clauses

eu-red-da.status: Applicable (expected to be superseded when the CRA fully applies — to be verified)
eu-red-da.scope: Internet-connected radio equipment. Harmonised standards EN 18031-1/2/3

red-en18031.title: Network protection, personal data protection and fraud prevention
red-en18031.text: Meet the EN 18031 series criteria (access control, secure updates, secure storage, etc.).

actions.dev: Signed firmware updates; no default passwords
actions.sales: Confirm the EU launch schedule for radio products

jp-meti-sbom.name: METI Guide on Introducing SBOM for Software Management Ver. 2.0
jp-meti-sbom.authority: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
jp-meti-sbom.scope: Software suppliers and purchasers. Ver. 2.0 adds a vulnerability management process and a model for SBOM responsibility allocation in contracts

meti-process.title: SBOM adoption phases
meti-process.text: Adopt SBOM in phases: environment setup → creation and sharing → operation and management (including vulnerability management).

actions.dev: Decide on SBOM generation tools and format

meti-contract.title: Clarify SBOM responsibilities in contracts
meti-contract.text: Define the scope of SBOM creation, delivery format and vulnerability response responsibilities in contracts.

actions.sales: Include SBOM scope and response responsibility clauses in contracts with Japanese customers

jp-esa.name: Economic Security Promotion Act — Ensuring Stable Provision of Specified Essential Infrastructure Services
jp-esa.binding: Mandatory (designated social infrastructure operators) → supplier information submission
jp-esa.scope: Designated social infrastructure operators in sectors such as electricity, telecommunications and finance must notify in advance information on constituent equipment, parts and outsourcees when introducing critical facilities
dates: Prior screening of critical facilities takes effect

esa-info.title: Provide information on constituent equipment, parts and suppliers
esa-info.text: Provide information on components, manufacturers and subcontracting so that the customer (operator) can file its notification.

actions.dev: Complete supplier information in the SBOM
actions.admin: Maintain lists of partners and subcontractors
actions.sales: Confirm submission materials when delivering to Japanese infrastructure customers

jp-jcstar.name: JC-STAR (IoT Product Security Conformity Assessment Scheme)
jp-jcstar.binding: Recommended (may be required in government/corporate procurement)
jp-jcstar.status: Operating (started with ★1; higher levels being introduced progressively — to be verified)

jcstar-1.title: Minimum security requirements
jcstar-1.text: No default passwords, provision of updates, vulnerability reporting point of contact, disclosure of support period, etc.

actions.dev: Update capability and secure defaults
actions.sales: Use label acquisition in sales in Japan

jp-gov-std.name: Common Standards for Cybersecurity Measures for Government Agencies
jp-gov-std.authority: Cabinet cybersecurity organization (successor to NISC — to be verified)
jp-gov-std.status: In force (revised annually — check for the latest edition)
jp-gov-std.scope: Japanese government agencies and procurement of their information systems. Includes supply chain risk management and software procurement requirements

jpgov-sc.title: Supply chain security requirements in procurement
jpgov-sc.text: Include security requirements for contractors and products (development controls, vulnerability response, absence of unauthorized functions, etc.) in procurement specifications.

actions.admin: Prepare a compliance matrix for security requirements in procurement specifications
actions.sales: Check specifications of Japanese public tenders

jp-med.name: Cybersecurity of Medical Devices (applying JIS T 81001-5-1)
jp-med.authority: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
jp-med.scope: Medical devices marketed in Japan. Cybersecurity added to the Essential Principles; conformity to JIS T 81001-5-1 required
dates: JIS T 81001-5-1 conformity requirement applies (to be verified)

jpmed-sbom.title: SBOM creation and vulnerability management
jpmed-sbom.text: Create an SBOM and establish a postmarket vulnerability management system.

actions.dev: SBOM and vulnerability management records
actions.sales: Confirm delivery requirements for Japanese medical institutions

kr-swsc.name: Software Supply Chain Security Guideline 1.0 (Korea)
kr-swsc.authority: Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT), National Intelligence Service (NIS) and Presidential Committee on Digital Platform Government
kr-swsc.binding: Recommended (may be required in public-sector procurement)
kr-swsc.status: In force (1.0) — subsequent revisions and pilot projects to be verified
kr-swsc.scope: Software developers, suppliers and acquiring organizations (public and private)

kr-swsc-sbom.title: Create, manage and provide SBOMs
kr-swsc-sbom.text: Create and manage SBOMs during development and provide them upon request from the acquiring organization.

actions.dev: Generate and attach an SBOM for every release
actions.admin: Manage SBOM retention and delivery history
actions.sales: State the SBOM delivery plan in public-sector proposals

kr-swsc-vuln.title: Component vulnerability management
kr-swsc-vuln.text: Identify and remediate component vulnerabilities based on the SBOM and share the results.

actions.dev: Remediate vulnerabilities and publish VEX

kr-swsc-integrity.title: Ensure distribution integrity
kr-swsc-integrity.text: Ensure integrity (signing and verification) across development, build and distribution.

actions.dev: Sign releases
actions.sales: Explain verification methods to customers

kr-n2sf.name: National Network Security Framework (N2SF) Security Guideline
kr-n2sf.binding: Mandatory (public institutions) → security requirements on supplied products
kr-n2sf.status: In force (official edition and application schedule to be verified)
kr-n2sf.scope: Classifies public institutions' information services into Classified (C), Sensitive (S) and Open (O) grades and applies security controls per grade. Requirements flow down to supplied software and cloud services
dates: Official edition of the guideline released (to be verified)

n2sf-sc.title: Supply chain security controls for acquired software
n2sf-sc.text: Manage the components, vulnerabilities and integrity of software introduced into information services of each grade.

actions.dev: Provide SBOMs and signatures
actions.admin: Materials for the acquiring organization's security review
actions.sales: Confirm public-sector customers' requirements by grade (C/S/O)

kr-ismsp.name: ISMS-P Certification Criteria (Personal Information & Information Security Management System)
kr-ismsp.authority: Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) and Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) (KISA)
kr-ismsp.binding: Mandatory (businesses above a size threshold) → supplier management
kr-ismsp.scope: Companies subject to mandatory certification (customers) inspect external party and development security and request evidence from suppliers
dates: Integrated ISMS-P certification criteria in effect

ismsp-23.title: External party security requirements and inspection
ismsp-23.text: Customers contractually require and inspect external software and service providers' implementation of security requirements.

actions.sales: Check special security terms in contracts

ismsp-28.title: Security requirements and testing for acquired software
ismsp-28.text: Define and test security requirements at acquisition; manage vulnerabilities in open source software.

actions.dev: Provide security test results and SBOMs

ismsp-2108.title: Patch management
ismsp-2108.text: Apply software security patches in a timely manner (customer side). Suppliers must provide patch information.

kr-fin.name: Regulation on Supervision of Electronic Financial Transactions and Financial-Sector SW Supply Chain Security Requirements
kr-fin.authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC), Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and Financial Security Institute (FSI)
kr-fin.status: In force (follow-up measures on network separation reform and SBOM to be verified)
kr-fin.scope: Companies supplying software to financial companies. Detailed items are assessed against the financial sector inspection checklist (uploaded)
dates: Financial sector network separation reform roadmap announced

krfin-checklist.title: Financial sector supply chain inspection items
krfin-checklist.text: Assess each item of the uploaded financial sector checklist (Admin console › Regulatory compliance verification).

actions.dev: Evidence for development-phase checklist items
actions.sales: Confirm financial customers' inspection schedules

kr-secure-coding.name: Guidelines for Building and Operating Information Systems of Public Agencies — Software Security Development
kr-secure-coding.authority: Ministry of the Interior and Safety (MOIS)
kr-secure-coding.scope: Software developed in IT projects of administrative and public institutions. Removal and diagnosis of security weaknesses
dates: Secure software development made mandatory (expanded in phases)

kr-sc-weak.title: Remove and diagnose security weaknesses
kr-sc-weak.text: Remove security weaknesses according to the design and implementation-phase security weakness criteria, and submit the diagnosis results.

actions.dev: Diagnose and fix security weaknesses with static analysis
actions.sales: Include in the deliverables list of public-sector projects

kr-cc.name: Security Conformity Verification and CC Certification (public-sector procurement of security products)
kr-cc.authority: National Intelligence Service (NIS) and KISA (IT Security Certification Center)
kr-cc.binding: Mandatory (information security products procured by public institutions)
kr-cc.scope: Information security products and network equipment introduced into public institutions

kr-cc-cert.title: Determine whether certification/verification is required
kr-cc-cert.text: Determine, by product type, whether CC certification or a security function confirmation certificate is required.

actions.sales: Confirm public tender eligibility requirements

kr-csap.name: Cloud Security Assurance Program (CSAP)
kr-csap.authority: Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) and KISA
kr-csap.binding: Procurement condition (certification public bodies must give priority to)
kr-csap.scope: Companies supplying cloud (IaaS/SaaS) services to public institutions

csap-sc.title: Security management of service components
csap-sc.text: Manage vulnerabilities, patches and the supply chain of the software that makes up the service.

actions.dev: Manage SBOMs for SaaS components
actions.sales: Confirm certification grade when selling SaaS to the public sector

uk-psti.scope: Consumer connectable products sold in the UK

psti-req.title: Three core requirements
psti-req.text: Ban on default or universal passwords, publication of a point of contact for reporting vulnerabilities, publication of the minimum security update period.

actions.dev: Remove default passwords
actions.admin: Publish the reporting contact and support period
actions.sales: Include the statement of compliance

in-certin-sbom.binding: Recommended (required in government and essential-sector procurement)
in-certin-sbom.scope: Companies supplying software to Indian public and essential sectors

certin-fields.title: SBOM fields and updates
certin-fields.text: Include component information (supplier, version, license, hash, etc.) and have update and sharing procedures in place.

actions.dev: Complete license and hash fields in the SBOM
actions.sales: Confirm Indian public tender requirements
